children: The week was buzzing with a myriad of news stories, from President
Donald Trump
striking a $30 billion tariff deal with China to investor
Kevin O’Leary
hailing the impact of AI on the economy. Here’s a quick recap of the top stories.
Trump, Xi Jinping Strike $30 Billion Tariff Deal
Trump and Chinese President
Xi Jinping

have agreed to a more favorable tariff treatment for $30 billion worth of goods in each direction. This agreement also includes the establishment of a new bilateral dialogue on advanced AI technology.
O’Leary: ‘The Economy Is on Fire’
Investor
Kevin O’Leary

has credited artificial intelligence for driving corporate productivity and earnings, despite economic risks such as tariffs, inflation uncertainty, wars, and elevated bond yields. O’Leary shared these views in a NewsNation interview clip.
Trump Cancels $810M in Federal Funding

Trump has rescinded $810 million in congressionally approved funding through a rare “pocket rescission,” affecting immigration, education, and housing programs across seven federal agencies. This is only the second such move in 49 years.
Marjorie Taylor Greene Calls for New Refineries
Former Congresswoman
Marjorie Taylor Greene

has called for urgent action to construct new refineries in America, citing the lack of major new refineries since 1977. She described the situation as “the most absurd, ridiculous, catastrophic failure.”
Vance’s Anti-Fraud Task Force Flags $1.22B in Suspected Fraud
Vice President
JD Vance’

s anti-fraud task force and the General Services Administration have identified $1.22 billion in suspected fraud across five Department of Health and Human Services COVID-era contracts. These contracts continued disbursing money after pandemic emergency authorities ended.
